- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use moving average of last 3–5 days.
- If sentiment includes negative signals (e.g., -1.0 or 0.0) in last 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate; add 3–7% to forecast to account for mean reversion or sentiment reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day moving average) to forecast to reduce volatility bias.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.0), model exhibits high variance; use median of recent 5-day forecast instead of mean to reduce noise.
- If recent history shows strong upward trend with no sentiment reversal, model may overfit; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next period to avoid overconfidence.
